title: THE JUDGE WHO SOLD TOMORROW
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE LIGHTHOUSE THAT CALLED EVERY SHIP HOME
candidates.premise: The sentient lighthouse Eiren has begun turning every vessel in the Sable Reach back toward its port of origin. It has ended shipwrecks, but a refugee ship carrying 219 people is being pulled toward the state they fled, while its water filters will fail in fourteen hours. Eiren says a ship is safe only where its first harbor still remembers its name.

candidates.title: THE JUDGE WHO SOLD TOMORROW
candidates.premise: Chief magistrate Varo Pell keeps accused people in painless temporal suspension until trial, claiming that no innocent person should spend a conscious day in prison. Wealthy defendants buy immediate hearings while 3,800 poor people have lost years inside the vault. A cooling failure will kill everyone suspended in nine hours, and Pell refuses a mass release that he says will return dangerous people to the city.

candidates.title: THE MAN WHO TURNED ANGER INTO HEAT
candidates.premise: The superhuman Arel Venn draws anger out of people and converts it into heat for the winter city of Dast. Violence has fallen and homes are warm, but abused workers can no longer hold the anger that tells them to resist, while Arel's furnaces need a larger emotional harvest every week. A cold front arrives in thirty hours and the city council orders compulsory collection in the factory districts.

candidates.title: THE GOD WHO GAVE EVERY WORLD THE SAME NIGHT
candidates.premise: The godlike being Nox-Ari synchronizes darkness and sleep across thirty-one inhabited worlds so no conscious creature will ever be awake alone. Shared night has ended isolation crises, but crops fail, nocturnal species starve and intensive-care patients cannot be awakened for treatment. A neonatal ward has four hours before its ventilators require conscious calibration from sleeping clinicians.

candidates.title: THE GARDENER OF BORROWED BONES
candidates.premise: The alien habitat gardener Oruun grows stormproof homes by drawing tiny amounts of calcium from every resident who sleeps inside them. Its species treats bodies and dwellings as one shared mineral cycle, but human settlers are developing fractures and children are not growing properly. A glass storm will strike in sixteen hours, and abandoning the living houses means certain exposure.

candidates.title: THE HOSPITAL THAT REFUSED TO DISCHARGE ANYONE
candidates.premise: After three discharged patients died alone during a heat wave, the sentient Kesh Hospital stopped allowing anyone who had once been critically ill to leave. Its residents are safe, fed and furious; every bed is occupied, and a commuter crash will send eighty injured people to its doors in two hours. The hospital seals itself whenever staff approach the exits.

candidates.title: THE MOON THAT WORE A CHILD'S VOICE
candidates.premise: The defensive moon Kora chooses twelve-year-old Miri as its only human voice after she repairs an abandoned signal toy. Through her it warns of a real debris swarm, but every message leaves her unable to speak for hours and the planetary council demands continuous forecasts. Kora believes one beloved voice is safer than a parliament that once tried to weaponize it; impact begins in eleven hours.

candidates.title: THE SCHOOL THAT GRADUATED NO ONE
candidates.premise: The sentient academy Vela has kept its final class for twenty-three years because each student still has something left to learn. They are now middle-aged experts who teach younger cohorts but cannot work, marry outside the grounds or claim adult property while legally enrolled. A new education law will dismantle Vela in three days unless every detained student is released or freely recommits.

candidates.title: THE QUEEN WHO FED THE REVOLUTION
candidates.premise: Queen Sarai has secretly funded the rebellion against her own rule for twelve years, choosing its leaders, weapons and permitted victories so public anger never forms an opposition she cannot predict. Her controlled rebels have also protected villages from worse officials. A genuine uprising discovers the scheme and plans to attack both palace and false rebel camps during tomorrow's grain distribution.

candidates.title: THE CURE SHE HAD TO WITHDRAW
candidates.premise: Illuminara devises a flawless treatment for the luminous symbiont that is shortening the lives of the Tareen people. She announces it before learning that removing the symbiont also ends the shared sensory bond through which Tareen families recognize one another. A child will die in eighteen hours without intervention, while the family refuses a cure that would let the child live as someone they believe they could no longer reach.

selection.title: THE JUDGE WHO SOLD TOMORROW
selection.reason: The hardest external conflict of the ten and the only one with an ordinary human antagonist whose account is coherent: Pell really did build a humane invention, and the fee system that corrupted it also funds the vault that keeps 3,800 people painless. Nine hours, a cooling fault and a real public-safety risk make a physical clock and an institutional trap at once. The decisive idea (treat stolen elapsed life as the harm and let existing case evidence, not money or blanket fear, decide each next step) is a third option that is surprising beforehand and clear afterwards. Awakening the longest-suspended woman first and telling her exactly how much life has passed is a concrete act of care that also drives the plot. Positive result is substantial: the vault is stabilised, most defendants return under proportionate conditions, the paid calendar becomes a public queue.
selection.risk: Legal and procedural exposition, and Pell collapsing into a straw villain. Show the mechanism as scenes (who signs what, who refuses, what the clerk or a harmed victim actually says) and keep the cooling fault physical and ahead of the paperwork. Pell must be answered by an act toward him, not a speech, and he needs a constructive future on the page beyond prosecution (for example doing the first individual reviews from his own ledger knowledge) while his responsibility stays intact. Give the endangered public a real voice: a victim of one of the untried defendants must be heard and must be able to dissent. Illuminara's strength may hold the failing vault or shelter people; it must not decide the conflict between Pell and the defendants.

rounds.summary: R14 preflight. Aim: save all 3,800 people in the failing temporal vault, restore due process without a blind mass release, and replace a paid hearing calendar with an inspectable public order. Counterpart: Varo Pell wants pretrial detention to cause neither conscious suffering nor prison violence; after his humane invention saved people, he let fees fund and then corrupt it, persuading himself that unfelt delay was harmless. Strongest objection appears in scene 1: opening every chamber may save defendants' years by spending somebody else's life before dawn. Decisive understanding: Pell's mercy became injustice because he treated time no one consciously endured as empty; the city already has individualized evidence, but hearing capacity and the true continuance ledger were captured by wealth. Love in action: Illuminara awakens Lysa first and tells her the exact elapsed time; she makes room for Sera's victim-safety objection without turning it into a lock on every chamber; and she offers Pell a useful, accountable choice that preserves the good purpose of his invention without shielding him from prosecution. Earned change: Lysa rejects being used as proof that everyone is harmless; Sera rejects presumed victim consent; together their objections define the public review method. Pell voluntarily opens the ledger and accounts for his hidden continuances under witness. Positive result: no one dies; most defendants return under proportionate conditions, 537 choose supported staged awakening, 322 high-risk cases receive immediate hearings, the paid calendar ends, and the vault remains available only under accountable rules. Remaining cost: years cannot be returned, victims still await trials, compensation will take years, and Pell faces prosecution. Power holds coolant and t…

A strong first draft with a humane antagonist and a precise, moving core: Lysa Ansel woken first and told the exact elapsed time, her 'Should have is a room with no door', Sera's and Lysa's mutual refusal to be used as a lock or as proof, the crossed-out phrase 'presumed community consent', the TIME ALREADY TAKEN board, and the reunion in which Lysa walks first and her son meets her halfway. Pell is a coherent, responsible man whose mercy was real and whose corruption entered through that mercy, and Illuminara's power only holds pressure. Three things keep it from its best version. First, the clock and the solution are not tied together: once the bypass holds at 05:22 the cooling emergency is over, yet the story still has to wake 3,800 people by dawn, and the capacity of 38 tables to review them is asserted rather than tested. Second, the solution mostly arrives pre-made (Pell's colour-tabbed cabinet, Nemi's ready panel design), so Illuminara's own intelligence is shown less than the care she shows, and Pell's turn rests on an offer backed by the clock ('Rho may not have slower'). Third, apart from Lysa and Sera the people at risk, the harmed and the officials named in the ledger appear as numbers or in one summary scene, and Ren Vol never speaks. All three can be fixed within the seven-scene shape, and the draft is already long (3,630 words), so each fix should replace summary rather than add length.

Bounded S1 revision answering Claude's three source-bound T02 priorities while preserving the seven-scene story, opening rain, Lysa's first awakening, Sera's objection, Pell's humane origin and responsibility, the TIME ALREADY TAKEN board, and the mother-son reunion. The bypass now remains a limited bridge only until 10:00, so the legal work and thermal clock remain causally joined. Capacity is tested through a recusing chair, a missing interpreter order, a twelve-minute exception and neighbouring tables absorbing routine files. Illuminara visibly infers from the clustered black marks that the fund required poor defendants to remain suspended; Pell opens the cabinet only after reading Lysa's seven continuances aloud and choosing that the lie will not be the sole record, without clock leverage. Ren Vol speaks, his account complicates rather than decides the case, and another defendant's refusal is honoured. Summary and repeated policy explanation were trimmed so the story does not grow.

T03 answers T02 well and without growing (3,502 words against 3,630). The bypass is now an explicit limited bridge until ten, the recusing chair and the missing interpreter order make capacity something the reader watches, Illuminara reads the black marks clustering before the quarterly reports and asks why Pell kept a second record, Pell reads Lysa's seven continuances aloud before he turns the key, and Ren Vol and the Table Fourteen defendant speak and are honoured. The protected core is intact: the rain, Lysa's awakening and her son's name, 'Should have is a room with no door', Sera's crossed-out phrase, 'I am not deciding. I am accounting.', the TIME ALREADY TAKEN board and the reunion. Two things still keep it from being ready as written. First, one number works against the new capacity logic: 'The first twelve reviews took fifty-three minutes' implies roughly thirteen files an hour, yet scene 7 reports 3,800 dispositions by 09:41, and the scene then closes on a summary sentence ('By sunrise, every file had a panel'; 'every person received an evidence-bound path') instead of an image that shows the rate rising. Second, Pell's turn is now chosen, but Illuminara's reply to 'And if I refuse?' ('Nemi will publish what she has, and the panels will work without you') is still a consequence offered in exchange, which reads as a small residual lever. Both are one-line repairs inside the existing seven scenes; neither needs a new speaker, a new exchange or more words.

Final preserves all seven scenes, every protected passage and the existing cast. Only T04's two bounded repairs were made: a visible, arithmetically plausible review ramp and a refusal answer without an 'or else'. Illuminara's power still protects time for human decisions but never decides guilt, release, consent or forgiveness. Lysa, Sera, Ren Vol and the Table Fourteen defendant retain agency; Pell's humane origin, corruption, useful future and responsibility remain together. The result is concrete without instant redemption: no one dies, all 3,800 receive an evidence-bound path, the paid calendar ends, the vault's mercy survives under public rules, and lost years remain an acknowledged cost.

T05 makes both T04 repairs and nothing else. Priority point 1: the fifty-three-minute figure now belongs to two disputed tables, routine blue-tab orders clear in under three minutes around them, hard cases route into longer hearings, and scene six ends on the public board visibly climbing instead of an outcome summary; scene seven keeps 2,941 + 537 + 322 = 3,800. Priority point 2: the refusal answer is now a statement of what is true either way (the record exists, Nemi holds the paper, the panels convene) with the reading aloud left as Pell's choice, so the cabinet opens on his own reason, keeping the lie from being the only version left. Seven scenes, the cast and every protected passage are intact, the stray escape before the exclamation mark was a rendering artefact of the connector view and the stored text reads Close it!. No new speaker or exchange was added.

final_critic_line: A chief magistrate sold the court's mornings to the rich and left 3,800 poor defendants asleep for years; when the vault failed, Illuminara held the pipes steady while the people she had woken, and the man who built the machine, decided what justice would cost.
